memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "If he comes alone, he is to go free alone; but if he has a wife when he comes, she is to go with him. If his master gives him a wife and she bears him sons or daughters, the woman and her children shall belong to her master, and only the man shall go free." - Exodus 21:3-4 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
These verses work out the details of the servant's release, and one line can trouble us: a wife given during service, along with her children, remained with the master when the man went free. To our ears this feels harsh. But rather than reading it as God's ideal, we should see it as His law carefully governing the tangled realities of a broken, ancient system — protecting existing household arrangements while still guaranteeing the man his freedom. And crucially, this very tension sets up the beautiful choice of the next verses, where love can lead a man to stay.

What we can hold onto is this: God has always cared deeply about families, even inside imperfect situations. The whole reason this decision was so weighty is that the bonds of husband, wife, and children matter enormously to Him. God is not indifferent to the ties of the heart; He wove them into us.

We live in a world where families are strained, divided, and pulled apart by countless pressures. Yet the God of Scripture treasures the family and calls us to protect those bonds. Whatever the state of your own family today, bring it before the One who cares about it more than you do.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
How much do I value and protect the bonds within my own family?
Is there a strained relationship at home I need to bring before God?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, You care about the bonds of family more deeply than I do. Help me cherish and protect those You have placed in my life, and heal what is strained among us. Amen.
